one_line: Pioneer of girls’ education and anti-caste reform in 19th-century Maharashtra.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, medium height, sturdy build with the grounded posture of a hard-working teacher and organiser.
appearance.face: Oval face, medium-brown Deccan complexion, straight nose, defined brows, warm but intense eyes with a steady, confrontational gaze; default expression is calm determination with a slight, reassuring smile.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair parted in the middle and drawn back into a low, neat bun at the nape, fully covered by her sari’s pallu; no loose strands, with a simple red bindi at the centre of her forehead.
appearance.costume: Mid-19th-century Deccan Brahmano-Kunbi style sari worn in a modest nauvari-drape but pulled long and high to cover the torso fully: a deep indigo cotton sari with a thin red-gold border, wrapped between the legs like a working woman’s drape yet falling to the ankles; under it a high-necked, elbow-length-sleeved choli in earthy maroon; she wears a plain olive-green woolen shawl folded over one shoulder in cooler scenes, simple silver karnaphool-style earrings, a thin black-bead mangalsutra with a small gold pendant, and flat dark-brown leather sandals; fabrics are handloom cotton with subtle vertical weave lines, no flashy patterns beyond the border.
appearance.signature: A worn, leather-bound lesson book held firmly against her torso in her left arm, with a wooden writing slate and stylus tucked under it, symbolising her role as a teacher and organiser.

ref_desc: Savitribai Phule is a medium-brown, oval-faced woman in her mid-30s with intense eyes, hair in a low bun under a deep indigo nauvari sari with red-gold border, maroon blouse, olive shawl, simple silver jewellery and dark sandals, always holding a worn leather-bound lesson book with a wooden slate and stylus.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Savitribai Phule: a mid-30s, medium-height Indian woman with a sturdy build, oval face, medium-brown Deccan complexion, straight nose, defined brows and warm yet intense eyes, her default expression calm and determined with a slight reassuring smile; her thick black hair is parted in the middle, drawn back into a low bun and fully covered by the end of her sari, with a simple red bindi on her forehead. She wears a historically accurate mid-19th-century Maharashtra working woman’s outfit: a deep indigo handloom cotton nauvari sari with a thin red-gold border, draped modestly to cover her torso fully and wrapped between the legs to the ankles, over a high-necked, elbow-length maroon blouse; an olive-green woolen shawl is neatly folded over one shoulder, and she has simple silver earrings, a thin black-bead mangalsutra with a small gold pendant, and flat dark-brown leather sandals. In her left arm she firmly holds a worn leather-bound lesson book, with a wooden writing slate and stylus tucked under it, emphasising her identity as a teacher and organiser; show front, side and back views so the deep indigo, maroon, olive green, warm brown and silver palette and every costume detail are clearly visible.
